name: Emancipator: Baralku
intro: What started as a university project on identity and the thumbprint became the cover of Emancipator’s fifth studio album, and the visual thread running through the record, the vinyl and the merch line.
credit: Album and music © Emancipator / Loci Records.

chapters.label: 01 — The idea
chapters.heading: A thumbprint is the one mark that is only ever yours.
text: The project began at university with a brief around identity. I kept coming back to the thumb: the print as a signature nobody can copy, and a record of everything that shapes a person. I built a series of prints out of other materials: street maps of a city, the grain of a tree.
In the tree-ring version the ridges read as growth over time, and placing the print where a face should be swapped a portrait for something more personal than a face could show.
chapters.caption: From the original series: a thumbprint built from a city street map, identity shaped by place.

chapters.label: 02 — From brief to record
chapters.heading: An island in the stars
text: Baralku is named after the spirit island of Yolngu belief, where departed souls light fires in the Milky Way. The faceless figure against a dark, star-flecked ground fitted that story: one individual, reduced to the mark only they leave behind.
The palette stays restrained, cold blue ridges warmed by a copper edge, with small, wide-tracked type so the image does the work at thumbnail size on streaming platforms as well as on a 12" sleeve.
chapters.caption: The full Baralku artwork without typography.

apps_text: The thumbprint became the album’s identity across vinyl, digital and the official merch range, licensed to Emancipator Music for ongoing use.
